parts.text:
34 A filament lamp has a resistance of 180 Ω when the current in it is 500 mA.
What is the power dissipated in the lamp?
A
45 W
B
90 W
C
290 W
D
360 W

hints: Convert the lamp current from $500\text{ mA}$ to amperes before substituting, since $1\text{ mA} = 10^{-3}\text{ A}$.
You are given $I$ and $R$ for the $180\text{ }\Omega$ filament, so use the power form $P = I^2R$ rather than needing voltage first.
Square the current in amperes to get $0.25\text{ A}^2$, then multiply by $180\text{ }\Omega$ and check the result is in watts.
walkthrough: Identify the givens: resistance $R = 180\text{ }\Omega$ and current $I = 500\text{ mA}$ for the filament lamp.
Convert current to SI units: $I = 500\text{ mA} = 500 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A} = 0.50\text{ A}$.
State the governing relation when $I$ and $R$ are known: electrical power dissipated is $P = I^2R$.
Calculate and check units: $P = 45\text{ W}$, and $\text{A}^2\Omega = \text{W}$ so the unit is correct.

B.explanation: 90 is the p.d. across the lamp, $V = IR = 0.50 \times 180 = 90\text{ V}$, not the power $I^2R$.

C.explanation: 290 W does not satisfy $P = I^2R$ for $0.50\text{ A}$ and $180\text{ }\Omega$ and is far larger than $45\text{ W}$.

D.explanation: 360 W is 8 times too large and would need about $1.41\text{ A}$ in $180\text{ }\Omega$, not the given $0.50\text{ A}$.
